chapter.v:
Better is
a dry morsel with quietness,Than a house full of feasting with strife. [Is. 47:7-9 b 1 Kin. 4:21; Ezra]

A wise
servant will rule over a son who causes shame,And will share an inheritance among the brothers. [Jer. 13:17] [Job 7:3]

The refining
pot is for silver and the furnace for gold,But the Lord tests the hearts. [Lam. 2:9 g Deut. dismay (see 2:1; 4:1; Is. 1:21; 14:4; Jer. 9:19; 48:17; Ezek. 26:17). Jerusalem is personified, or portrayed as a person (see Is. 1:21).] [Jer. 52:27]

An evildoer
gives heed to false lips;A liar listens eagerly to a spiteful tongue. [Is. 27:10]

He who
mocks the poor reproaches his Maker;He who is glad at calamity will not go unpunished. [Jer. 30:14, 15; Dan. 9:7, 16 k Jer.] [Deut. 28:43]

Children’s children
are the crown of old men,And the glory of children is their father.

Excellent speech
is not becoming to a fool,Much less lying lips to a prince. [Ps. 137:1]

A present
is a precious stone in the eyes of its possessor;Wherever he turns, he prospers. [[1 Kin. 8:46]] [Jer. 13:22; Ezek. 16:37; Hos. 2:10]

He who
covers a transgression seeks love,But he who repeats a matter separates friends. [Deut. 32:29; Is. 47:7; Jer. 5:31]

Rebuke is
more effective for a wise manThan a hundred blows on a fool. [Ps. 74:4-8; Is. 64:10, 11; Jer. 51:51 q Deut. 23:3; Neh. 13:1]

An evil
man seeks only rebellion;Therefore a cruel messenger will be sent against him.

Let a
man meet a bear robbed of her cubs,Rather than a fool in his folly. [Dan. 9:12]

Whoever rewards
evil for good,Evil will not depart from his house. [Ezek. 12:13;]

The beginning
of strife is like releasing water;Therefore stop contention before a quarrel starts. [Deut. 28:48] [1 Sam. 12:14,]

He who
justifies the wicked, and he who condemns the just,Both of them alike are an abomination to the Lord. [Is. 63:3; [Rev.]

Why is
there in the hand of a fool the purchase price of wisdom,Since he has no heart for it? [Ps. 69:20; Eccl. 4:1; Jer. 13:17; Lam. 2:18]

A friend
loves at all times,And a brother is born for adversity. [[Is. 1:15]; Jer. 4:31 y 2 Kin. 24:2-4; Jer. 12:9 5 Prays]

A man
devoid of understanding shakes hands in a pledge,And becomes surety for his friend. [Neh. 9:33; Ps. 119:75; Dan. 9:7,]

He who
loves transgression loves strife,And he who exalts his gate seeks destruction.

He who
has a deceitful heart finds no good,And he who has a perverse tongue falls into evil. [Job 30:27; Is. 16:11; Jer. 4:19; Lam. 2:11; Hos. 11:8 c Deut. 32:25;]

He who
begets a scoffer does so to his sorrow,And the father of a fool has no joy. [Is. 13; [Jer. 46]]

A merry
heart does good, like medicine,But a broken spirit dries the bones. [Neh. 4:4, 5; Ps. Jer. 30:16]

A wicked
man accepts a bribe behind the backTo pervert the ways of justice.

Wisdom is
in the sight of him who has understanding,But the eyes of a fool are on the ends of the earth.

A foolish
son is a grief to his father,And bitterness to her who bore him.

Also, to
punish the righteous is not good,Nor to strike princes for their uprightness.

He who
has knowledge spares his words,And a man of understanding is of a calm spirit.

Even a
fool is counted wise when he holds his peace;When he shuts his lips, he is considered perceptive.
